name: HIPAA Security Rule
description: Administrative, physical, and technical safeguards for electronic health information. Titles and summaries are our own short wording, not the regulation text.

requirements.title: Administrative safeguards
requirements.summary: How the organization assigns security work and keeps the program running.

children.title: Security management
children.summary: The organization looks for risks to health information and reduces them.

children.title: Workforce security
children.summary: People get access only when their role needs it, and access ends when they leave.

children.title: Information access
children.summary: Access to health information follows a written rule for who may see it.

children.title: Security awareness
children.summary: The workforce is reminded how to protect health information.

children.title: Security incidents
children.summary: Security incidents are found, reported, and followed through.

children.title: Contingency plan
children.summary: The organization can keep going and recover health information after a disruption.

children.title: Evaluation
children.summary: The security program is checked against how the organization actually works.

requirements.title: Physical safeguards
requirements.summary: How rooms, devices, and media that hold health information are protected.

children.title: Facility access
children.summary: Only the right people can enter spaces that hold systems with health information.

children.title: Device and media
children.summary: Devices and media that hold health information are tracked and wiped before reuse.

requirements.title: Technical safeguards
requirements.summary: How systems control, record, and protect access to health information.

children.title: Access control
children.summary: Systems allow a person to reach only the health information their role needs.

children.title: Audit controls
children.summary: Systems record activity so the organization can review who did what.

children.title: Integrity
children.summary: Health information is protected from improper change or destruction.

children.title: Person authentication
children.summary: A system checks that the person asking for access is who they claim to be.

children.title: Transmission security
children.summary: Health information sent over a network is guarded against being read or changed.
